## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] llama3.1 library tags follow <size>-<instruct|text>-<quant>, with suffixes q2_K, q3_K_S/M/L, q4_0, q4_1, q4_K_S/M, q5_0, q5_1, q5_K_S/M, q6_K, q8_0 and fp16; the page lists 93 tags, sizes from 3.2GB (8b q2_K) to 812GB (405b fp16). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://ollama.com/library/llama3.1/tags · keywords: Ollama model quantization tags and library variants · also: https://ollama.com/library/gemma3/tags
- [statement] llama3.1:latest, llama3.1 and llama3.1:8b are the same model (4.9GB, ID 46e0c10c039e). The page does not name its quantization, but the ID matches llama3.1:8b-instruct-q4_K_M, so the default is most likely Q4_K_M. gemma3:latest (3.4GB) likewise shares a digest with gemma3:4b-it-q4_K_M. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://ollama.com/library/llama3.1/tags · keywords: Ollama model quantization tags and library variants · also: https://ollama.com/library/gemma3/tags

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Tag sets differ per model: gemma3 offers -it-qat, -it-q4_K_M, -it-q8_0, -it-fp16 and -it-bf16 (270m has no q4_K_M tag), unlike llama3.1's K-quant ladder. Check the model's tags page before assuming a quant exists. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://ollama.com/library/gemma3/tags · keywords: Ollama model quantization tags and library variants · also: https://ollama.com/library/llama3.1/tags
- [statement] gemma3 -it-qat tags are quantization-aware-trained Q4_0-format builds from Google. Google reports a 54% reduction in perplexity drop versus post-training Q4_0 quantization (llama.cpp perplexity eval) and weight VRAM of 54GB BF16 to 14.1GB int4 for 27B. (medium confidence) — https://developers.googleblog.com/en/gemma-3-quantized-aware-trained-state-of-the-art-ai-to-consumer-gpus/ · keywords: Ollama model quantization tags and library variants · also: https://ollama.com/library/gemma3/tags

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Ollama's import docs say it does not quantize GGUF models during import; quantize first with a tool such as llama.cpp's llama-quantize. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/import · keywords: Ollama model quantization tags and library variants · also: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/quantize/README.md
- [statement] For Llama-3.1-8B, llama.cpp lists Q4_K_M at 4.89 bits/weight (4.58GiB, 71.9 t/s generation), Q5_K_M 5.70 bpw (5.33GiB, 67.2 t/s), Q8_0 8.50 bpw (7.95GiB, 50.9 t/s), F16 16.0 bpw (14.96GiB, 29.2 t/s). Smaller quants generate faster; the README gives no perplexity figures for them. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/quantize/README.md · keywords: Ollama model quantization tags and library variants
- [statement] llama.cpp advises that requantizing an already-quantized model can severely reduce quality, so start from a 16/32-bit GGUF, and that an importance matrix can reduce accuracy loss. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/quantize/README.md · keywords: Ollama model quantization tags and library variants
